correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md writes y=R0² as the larger root of P(y,x)=y²-[Ax²+B(1-x)²+C]y+ACx². At x<1, P(C,x)<0 and Py at the larger root is positive. Solving Px=0 with P=0 yields y=Ax and the unique interior critical x*=(B+C)/(A+B), admissible only A>C. x(p) increases from x0 to 1, proving all boundary cases and the stated p*. I independently used exact rational arithmetic to reproduce quadratic, x*=2/5, p*=5/8, threshold polynomial P(1,x(p))=[6-80(p-1/2)^2]/[25(5-4p)^2], and endpoint signs; the strict-subcritical set follows because the smaller root stays below C=3/5. Source’s 2026 paper supplies only the underlying next-generation expression. The p=1 reducible case is evaluated by continuity, not assumed human invasion.
